built_on: user's Docker Desktop (macOS), not the Claude authoring sandbox (no Docker there)
smoke_test_result: core-cpu1 launched, logged real CFE startup sequence, reached CFE_ES_Main entering OPERATIONAL state, then ran indefinitely until killed (SIGTERM) — confirmed working, real flight-software boot behavior
reproducibility_note: Independently verified 2026-08-03: a second, from-scratch Docker rebuild (`docker build --no-cache`, ~1 hour after the first) of core-cpu1 was NOT byte-identical — sha256 differed (41cffe62... vs cbffec77...). Root cause isolated precisely via `cmp -l` + `strings` diff, not assumed: of ~915KB total, exactly 22 bytes differ, in two locations. (1) Offsets 393508 and 393510 carry a literal embedded build-timestamp string baked into the binary by cFS's own build system — confirmed via a raw `strings` diff showing '202608031808' (first build) vs '202608031907' (second build), i.e. the two Docker builds' actual wall-clock times, ~59 minutes apart. (2) Offsets 889-908 (exactly 20 bytes = SHA-1 digest length) differ because they are the ELF .note.gnu.build-id section, which GNU ld's linker computes as a SHA-1 hash over the final linked binary's content — since (1) changes that content, the derived build-id legitimately changes too; it is a downstream consequence of the timestamp, not an independent source of non-determinism. Every other byte in the binary is identical across two independent from-scratch builds. See docs/Threat-Model.md 'Phase 7 reproducibility verification' for full methodology and STATUS.md 'Claims status' for exactly what this does and doesn't license claiming. Contrast with fprime-app/confirmed-build.json, whose real F´ build WAS bit-identical across the same test.
known_limitation: core-cpu1 is a long-running process (reaches OPERATIONAL state and loops forever managing the flight software bus), not a short-lived deterministic CLI program. Resolved (ISSUES-AND-FIXES-LOG.md ISSUE-003): src/health/health_check.py now uses a persistent-process strategy for this stack — launches the binary, watches stdout for the real 'CFE_ES_Main: CFE_ES_Main entering OPERATIONAL state' log line within a bounded window, then terminates it — so S3+ conditions (attestation, health check, rollback) can be exercised against this real binary. Individual test runs pass; a repeated-trial statistical evaluation against this real binary has not yet been done (still PRELIMINARY_INTERNAL_ONLY per STATUS.md).
